newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short sterling vols fall, puts popular.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short sterling vols fall, puts popular.

text.p: Implied volatility on short sterling options fell back slightly across the board on Friday in response to the absence of any decision on Thursday to raise British interest rates, traders said.

Ian Aubrey, head of futures and options sales at Yamaichi International (Europe), said March short sterling at-the-money futures options were trading at roughly 9.9 percent volatility, down from about 10.2 percent on Thursday.
LIFFE pages showed a burst of activity in June 92.75 puts where over 4,800 lots were traded by 1545 GMT, while over 2,800 lots of 93.25 changed hands.

"The majority of action in short sterling options was from one British institution buying one-by-two put spreads," said a trader at a Swiss house in London. "They bought the 93.25 strike and sold the 93.25 June puts."
The trader said the volatility on the 93.25 June puts was 11.5 percent and 13.5 percent on the 92.75 strike.
The slide in volatility was more marked in the March than the June series. June at-the-money volatility closed at 11.6 percent on Thursday.
"I expect (volatility) to keep firm," the trader said. "The uncertainty has increased now that the Tory government is in a minority."
Aubrey said the one-by-two put spread trade was a low-risk bearish transaction because the front part was bought at low volatility.
"People are putting on hedges in the quarterly month trading immediately after the 1997 election," said Aubrey.
He said they were betting on on an interest rate increase by June, which was far enough away that it was not too expensive to do.
